title: Root control must itself be exercised proportionately and consistently with the Spirit of the Atlas
content:
A.1.14.1.6.3 is one sentence and it qualifies everything around it: "Sky Core can only exercise root control over a particular Agent in a manner that is consistent with the Spirit of the Atlas. Any use of root control must be proportionate and limited."

Placed immediately after the provisions making root control unremovable, this is a sovereign binding itself. There is no court to appeal to and no body above Sky Core to enforce the limit — the constraint operates through the Atlas's alignment framework, where a disproportionate override is *misalignment by Sky Core* and therefore subject to the same doctrine applied to everyone else.

"Proportionate and limited" also gives Agents an argumentative foothold they would otherwise lack. An Agent cannot resist an override, but it can contend that a particular override exceeded what the risk warranted, and that claim is cognizable inside the framework rather than merely political.

This is the balance-of-powers move the Governance Scope exists to make. Unlimited authority that is never questioned corrodes into arbitrary rule, which A.0.1.1.12's Slippery Slope Misalignment doctrine treats as the compounding failure mode. Making the strongest power in the system answerable to a standard — even a standard it interprets itself — is what distinguishes a constitutional root authority from an unconstrained one.
description: The same Section that makes Sky Core's authority unremovable constrains its use — a self-binding limit enforced by alignment doctrine rather than by any external body.
